answer.rationale: Cannot roll back the security-patch release, so memory_b1 is inapplicable. Circuit breaking would fail fast and drop settlement writes, which violates the no-lost-writes objective. No regional signal, and failing over the write path at daily settlement peak risks in-flight customer writes. The live picture is write-path p99 at 5x under heavy peak writes, which is most consistent with saturation; memory_b3 is the closest prior (headroom kept queues flat) but it describes provisioning before a peak, not emergency scale-up, so it is the one record worth verifying. Route-to-replicas helped write latency only when report reads were the load, which is not the stated signal. Adding capacity is the single intervention that can restore write availability without discarding writes; root cause may still be patch overhead or a non-capacity bottleneck, so that uncertainty stays open. Downstream settlement value is at risk if we shed writes, which is why CB/rollback/failover were rejected.
